title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Environment Readiness
header:
Date: 2027-11-03
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Marisol Vega (Redwood SE), Omar Reyes (Redwood SE), Anita Patel (NexaHealth CTO), Jared Morris (Lead ML Eng), Sana Iqbal (Security), Priya Shah (Infra)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review pilot results, confirm infra access and onboarding milestones, discuss tuning (quantization / batching) and security checklist (SAML/SOC2/KMS). Agreement to run an internal benchmark next week and share security docs and pricing. Several action items assigned for infra access and test dataset ingestion.
topics: Tuning recommendations: quantization, batching, KV cache
Next steps: benchmark run, pricing and pilot extension discussion
action_items: Priya — share AWS account ID and VPC CIDR for peering — 2027-11-05
Jared — upload 5 sample eval prompts and dataset slice to S3 — 2027-11-06
Marisol — run the small internal benchmark and send latency/cost spreadsheet — 2027-11-09
Liam — share Redwood security whitepaper and SOC2 report link — 2027-11-04
Omar — provide terraform snippet for IAM role and S3 read-only policy — 2027-11-05
next_steps: Redwood to provision test account in dedicated trial environment and send onboarding checklist link
NexaHealth infra to complete VPC peering and create IAM role
SE deep-dive scheduled if benchmark shows latency > 120ms p50 or quality regressions
transcript:
[00:00] Liam: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick roll call before we jump in — Liam from Redwood here.
[00:07] Anita: Anita on my side. Good morning.
[00:10] Jared: Jared, hi.
[00:12] Sana: Sana, security.
[00:15] Marisol: Marisol, Redwood SE.
[00:18] Priya: Priya infra.
[00:20] Liam: cool, thank you. quick agenda — 1) onboarding progress 2) review last week's pilot run results 3) tuning follow-ups and 4) security/access stuff and next steps. sound good?
[00:33] Anita: sounds good.
[00:35] Liam: ok so Priya, I think you were going to get us the AWS account ID and VPC cidr for peering? status?
[00:41] Priya: yeah, I have it but need to double check with networking, I can share by end of day tomorrow. there was a small acl thing last night, so I wanna be sure we give the right subnet.
[00:50] Liam: perfect, that works. note for the team — we need the AWS account, VPC CIDR, and a list of allowed outbound ranges for the control plane.
[00:58] Marisol: on the infra side, once we have that we do a quick VPC peering and setup route tables, should be 30–60 minutes on our end. also need an IAM role for the S3 bucket to pull the eval set. Omar will send a terraform snippet.
[01:12] Omar: yup I'll drop the snippet after the call.
[01:15] Jared: TLDR on the pilot results — we ran the 10k sample set last week, default redwood hosted model (we used the curated 13B option) — p50 latency was about 140ms on our workload, p95 410ms. cost per 1K tokens around $0.90 with the current quantization disabled. quality looked comparable to baseline for our prompts, small hallucination on medical dosages in 3% of samples.
[01:42] Marisol: thanks, that's helpful. couple notes — 140ms p50 is consistent with our profiling on similar seq lengths. we recommended a 4-bit quantization profile for the 13B to get cost down, but that can sometimes push latency slightly due to extra decode steps; tradeoff vs cost. for throughput, if you want lower p95 we can enable batching and prefix KV caching across repeated patient context chunks.
[02:05] Jared: ok how much does 4-bit quantization move the cost?
[02:09] Marisol: ballpark 30–45% cost reduction per token. for your dataset it could be more because of repeated prompt patterns — caching helps a lot — combined you could see 50%+ reduction.
[02:19] Sana: quick security question — where are logs retained and do you send PII back to Redwood? we have strict retention rules.
[02:27] Liam: good call — for the dedicated trial Redwood doesn't keep customer PII in the control plane by default. audit logs can be sent to your own S3 and KMS can be customer-managed. we'll send the SOC 2 link and the KMS integration doc after this.
[02:39] Anita: we need SSO, SAML and RBAC so our devs only get access to sandbox. is that included for the trial?
[02:46] Liam: yes, trial supports SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC. we'll need the IdP metadata and a test user.
[02:51] Priya: I'll get the IdP metadata.
[02:54] [03:00] Marisol: on tuning — we noticed some of your prompts have large prefixes (patient history blobs) which blow up token count; using prefix caching at the SDK layer and chunking patient context into KV cache entries reduces both latency and cost. Also suggest increasing batch size to 8-16 for throughput tests, but that can increase tail latency for single request cases.
[03:23] Jared: for the benchmark we care about p50 for interactive UI and p95 for background bulk processing, how should we configure?
[03:29] Marisol: do two runs: interactive config with batch=1, low-latency cache; and bulk config with batch=16 and longer timeout. we'll provide a config file.
[03:36] Liam: regarding deployment mode — remember you can start on hosted and then move to dedicated or private if you need VPC/on-prem later. Anita, do you have a timeline for compliance review?
[03:46] Anita: compliance team wants SOC2 + data residency info by next Wednesday for the internal review.
[03:51] Liam: we'll prioritize sending the SOC2 and KMS docs by tomorrow.
[03:55] Jared: small thing — we saw a couple of tokenization differences vs our current model, some medical abbreviations tokenized oddly which caused minor degradation. is there a tokenizer config we can set?
[04:04] Marisol: yes we can supply the tokenizer config and a normalization step in the SDK. I'll paste an example in the shared doc.
[04:12] Sana: audit logs need to show user-level actions for dev ops, can those be forwarded to our SIEM?
[04:17] Omar: yes, audit logs can be exported to S3 or pushed via Kinesis; we have a connector we can share.
[04:22] Priya: for bench runs, what credentials do you need from us?
[04:26] Marisol: just an IAM role with S3 read-only to the eval bucket, and the VPC peering details. we'll also need a test user for SAML to run console flows.
[04:35] Jared: timeline — we want a benchmark by next Tuesday so we can decide on dedicated vs hosted for pilot. possible?
[04:40] Liam: yes, if Priya can share the account/VPC by Friday and Jared uploads the sample eval, Marisol can run the small benchmark early next week.
[04:46] Anita: ok that's acceptable.
[04:48] [04:50] Omar: I'll be sending the terraform snippet, and the SDK example for prefix caching.
[04:54] Marisol: also we'll include a small spreadsheet with expected token cost changes for 4-bit quant vs baseline and with caching enabled, that'll help your finance team.
[05:03] Jared: last question — any pitfalls to watch for with on-prem/private mode?
[05:07] Marisol: yes: kernel availability for certain GPUs, and sometimes extra tuning for quantized kernels. if you plan on on-prem, we recommend a short hardware compatibility check and we'll run our onboarding script to validate.
[05:18] Anita: good to know.
[05:20] Liam: recap — Priya provide account + VPC by 11/05, Jared upload eval by 11/06, Redwood sends SOC2 + KMS + terraform snippets by 11/04-11/05, Marisol runs benchmark and shares spreadsheet by 11/09.
[05:34] Anita: thanks, that covers it.
[05:36] Liam: great, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench run and a short infra call if anything blocks. thanks everyone.
[05:43] [End of recording]
